subject: math
title: Multiply Fractions
seo_title: Grade 5 Multiplying Fractions Worksheets: Area Models, Simplest Form, Mixed Numbers and Word Problems
standard_text: Apply and extend previous understandings of multiplication to multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction. Interpret the product (a/b) × q as a parts of a partition of q into b equal parts. Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling it with unit squares of the appropriate unit fraction side lengths, and show that the area is the same as would be found by multiplying the side lengths. Solve real world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers, e.g., by using visual fraction models or equations to represent the problem.
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 worksheets on multiplying fractions: find a fraction of a whole number, use area models for fraction × fraction, multiply tops and bottoms, simplify, multiply mixed numbers, find areas with fraction sides and solve recipe and part-of-a-part word problems. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Multiply the tops. Multiply the bottoms. Then simplify.
key_sub: × means “of”: 1/2 × 3/4 is half of 3/4, which is 3/8. Change mixed numbers to fractions first: 2 1/2 × 1 1/3 = 5/2 × 4/3 = 20/6 = 3 1/3.
body_html:
The big idea

In multiplication with fractions, × means “of.” 23 × 12 means 23 of 12. 12 × 34 means half of 34.

A fraction of a whole number

Split the whole number into equal parts (the bottom number), then take some of the parts (the top number).

A fraction of a fraction: the area model

Draw a square that is 1 whole. Shade one fraction as columns. Then take the other fraction of the shaded part as rows. The overlap is the answer.

The rule

Multiply the tops. Multiply the bottoms. Then simplify. The bottoms are multiplied because the square is cut into (bottom × bottom) equal parts.

ProblemMultiplySimplest form
23 × 45815815
34 × 2963616
34 × 61844 12

Tip: you can simplify before you multiply. In 34 × 29, divide 3 and 9 by 3 and divide 2 and 4 by 2: 12 × 13 = 16.

Mixed numbers and area

Change each mixed number to a fraction first. To find the area of a rectangle, multiply the side lengths.

Example

Find 2 12 × 1 13.

2 12 = 52 and 1 13 = 43. 52 × 43 = 206 = 103.

Answer: 3 13

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
12 × 34 = 34 (keeping a common bottom number)No common denominator needed: 38
12 × 34 = 46 (adding)Multiply the tops and the bottoms
2 12 × 1 13 = 2 16 (whole parts and fraction parts separately)Change to 52 × 43 first: 3 13
2 12 = 32 (adding the whole number to the top)2 × 2 + 1 = 5, so 2 12 = 52

faq.a: Multiply the numerators, multiply the denominators, then simplify. For example, 2/3 × 3/4 = 6/12 = 1/2.

faq.q: How do you multiply mixed numbers?
faq.a: Change each mixed number to an improper fraction, multiply, then simplify. For example, 2 1/2 × 1 1/3 = 5/2 × 4/3 = 20/6 = 3 1/3.

faq.q: What is an area model for multiplying fractions?
faq.a: Shade one fraction of a square as columns, then shade the other fraction of that part as rows; the overlap is the product. For 1/2 × 3/4, 3 of the 8 equal parts overlap, so the answer is 3/8.

faq.q: Why is the answer smaller when you multiply by a fraction?
faq.a: Multiplying by a fraction less than 1 means taking only part of a number. 1/2 × 3/4 is half of 3/4, so it is 3/8, which is less than 3/4.

items.q: The 12 counters are in 3 equal groups. What is 23 of 12?
items.e: Split 12 into 3 equal parts: 12 ÷ 3 = 4 in each part. Take 2 of the parts: 2 × 4 = 8. So 23 × 12 = 8. In the picture, 2 of the 3 groups are shaded.

items.q: The 16 counters are in 8 equal groups. What is 38 of 16?
items.e: Split 16 into 8 equal parts: 16 ÷ 8 = 2 in each part. Take 3 of the parts: 3 × 2 = 6. So 38 × 16 = 6. In the picture, 3 of the 8 groups are shaded.

items.q: The 15 counters are in 5 equal groups. What is 35 of 15?
items.e: Split 15 into 5 equal parts: 15 ÷ 5 = 3 in each part. Take 3 of the parts: 3 × 3 = 9. So 35 × 15 = 9. In the picture, 3 of the 5 groups are shaded.

items.q: The 21 counters are in 7 equal groups. What is 37 of 21?
items.e: Split 21 into 7 equal parts: 21 ÷ 7 = 3 in each part. Take 3 of the parts: 3 × 3 = 9. So 37 × 21 = 9. In the picture, 3 of the 7 groups are shaded.

items.q: The 10 counters are in 5 equal groups. What is 25 of 10?
items.e: Split 10 into 5 equal parts: 10 ÷ 5 = 2 in each part. Take 2 of the parts: 2 × 2 = 4. So 25 × 10 = 4. In the picture, 2 of the 5 groups are shaded.

items.q: The whole bar is 20. What is 35 × 20?
items.e: Split 20 into 5 equal parts: 20 ÷ 5 = 4 in each part. Take 3 of the parts: 3 × 4 = 12. So 35 × 20 = 12.

items.q: The whole bar is 24. What is 34 × 24?
items.e: Split 24 into 4 equal parts: 24 ÷ 4 = 6 in each part. Take 3 of the parts: 3 × 6 = 18. So 34 × 24 = 18.

items.q: The whole bar is 40. What is 58 × 40?
items.e: Split 40 into 8 equal parts: 40 ÷ 8 = 5 in each part. Take 5 of the parts: 5 × 5 = 25. So 58 × 40 = 25.

items.q: The whole bar is 28. What is 47 × 28?
items.e: Split 28 into 7 equal parts: 28 ÷ 7 = 4 in each part. Take 4 of the parts: 4 × 4 = 16. So 47 × 28 = 16.

items.q: 38 × 24 = ?
items.e: Split 24 into 8 equal parts: 24 ÷ 8 = 3 in each part. Take 3 of the parts: 3 × 3 = 9. So 38 × 24 = 9.

items.q: 36 × 34 = ?
items.e: Split 36 into 4 equal parts: 36 ÷ 4 = 9 in each part. Take 3 of the parts: 3 × 9 = 27. So 34 × 36 = 27. (You can also multiply first: 36 × 3 = 108, then 108 ÷ 4 = 27.)

items.q: Find 56 of 30.
items.e: Split 30 into 6 equal parts: 30 ÷ 6 = 5 in each part. Take 5 of the parts: 5 × 5 = 25. So 56 × 30 = 25.

items.q: 710 × 50 = ?
items.e: Split 50 into 10 equal parts: 50 ÷ 10 = 5 in each part. Take 7 of the parts: 7 × 5 = 35. So 710 × 50 = 35.

items.q: Find 29 of 45.
items.e: Split 45 into 9 equal parts: 45 ÷ 9 = 5 in each part. Take 2 of the parts: 2 × 5 = 10. So 29 × 45 = 10.

items.q: 48 × 512 = ?
items.e: Split 48 into 12 equal parts: 48 ÷ 12 = 4 in each part. Take 5 of the parts: 5 × 4 = 20. So 512 × 48 = 20. (You can also multiply first: 48 × 5 = 240, then 240 ÷ 12 = 20.)

items.e: Multiply the whole number by the top number and keep the bottom number: 5 × 2 = 10, so the product is 103. 10 ÷ 3 = 3 R 1, so 103 = 3 13.

items.e: Multiply the whole number by the top number and keep the bottom number: 6 × 3 = 18, so the product is 184. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 2: 184 = 92. 9 ÷ 2 = 4 R 1, so 92 = 4 12.

items.q: The square is 1 whole. The light columns are 34 of the square. Which multiplication does the dark part show?
c: 13 × 34
13 × 14
23 × 34
13 + 34
items.e: The light part is 3 of 4 columns: 34 of the square. The dark part is 1 of the 3 rows of the light part: 13 of it. So the dark part is 13 of 34, which is 13 × 34.

items.q: The model shows 12 × 34. What fraction of the whole square is dark?
items.e: The square is cut into 4 × 2 = 8 equal small rectangles. 3 × 1 = 3 of them are dark. So 12 × 34 = 38.

items.q: The model shows 34 × 23. What fraction of the whole square is one small rectangle?
items.e: There are 3 columns and 4 rows, so the square is cut into 3 × 4 = 12 equal parts. One part is 112. This is why you multiply the bottom numbers.

items.q: The model shows 23 × 35. What fraction of the whole square is one small rectangle?
items.e: There are 5 columns and 3 rows, so the square is cut into 5 × 3 = 15 equal parts. One part is 115. This is why you multiply the bottom numbers.

items.q: The model shows 34 × 45. How many small rectangles are dark, out of how many in all?
items.e: Dark: 4 columns × 3 rows = 12 small rectangles. In all: 5 columns × 4 rows = 20. So 34 × 45 = 1220.

items.q: The model shows 45 × 23. How many small rectangles are dark, out of how many in all?
items.e: Dark: 2 columns × 4 rows = 8 small rectangles. In all: 3 columns × 5 rows = 15. So 45 × 23 = 815.

items.q: The model shows 12 × 58. How many small rectangles are dark, out of how many in all?
items.e: Dark: 5 columns × 1 row = 5 small rectangles. In all: 8 columns × 2 rows = 16. So 12 × 58 = 516.

items.q: Which product is equal to 35 × 47?

53 × 74

items.e: Both products have tops 3 × 4 = 12 and bottoms 5 × 7 = 35, so both equal 1235. Swapping the top numbers does not change the answer.

sets.title: Area with fraction sides and mixed numbers

items.q: The big square is 1 ft on each side. What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: The square is cut into 4 × 3 = 12 tiles, so each tile is 112 sq ft. The shaded rectangle has 3 × 2 = 6 tiles: 612 sq ft. That is the same as 34 × 23 = 612. In simplest form, that is 12 sq ft.

items.q: The big square is 1 m on each side. What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: The square is cut into 5 × 4 = 20 tiles, so each tile is 120 sq m. The shaded rectangle has 2 × 3 = 6 tiles: 620 sq m. That is the same as 25 × 34 = 620. In simplest form, that is 310 sq m.

items.q: The big square is 1 yd on each side. What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: The square is cut into 6 × 2 = 12 tiles, so each tile is 112 sq yd. The shaded rectangle has 5 × 1 = 5 tiles: 512 sq yd. That is the same as 56 × 12 = 512.

items.q: The big square is 1 ft on each side. What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: The square is cut into 3 × 4 = 12 tiles, so each tile is 112 sq ft. The shaded rectangle has 2 × 1 = 2 tiles: 212 sq ft. That is the same as 23 × 14 = 212. In simplest form, that is 16 sq ft.

items.q: A rectangular garden bed is 56 m long and 35 m wide. What is its area? Write the answer in simplest form.
items.e: Area = length × width = 56 × 35. Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 56 × 35 = 1530. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 15: 1530 = 12 sq m.

items.q: A rectangular tray is 78 ft long and 23 ft wide. What is its area? Write the answer in simplest form.
items.e: Area = length × width = 78 × 23. Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 78 × 23 = 1424. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 2: 1424 = 712 sq ft.

items.q: A rectangular rug is 34 yd long and 49 yd wide. What is its area? Write the answer in simplest form.
items.e: Area = length × width = 34 × 49. Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 34 × 49 = 1236. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 12: 1236 = 13 sq yd.

items.q: A rectangular window is 910 m long and 56 m wide. What is its area? Write the answer in simplest form.
items.e: Area = length × width = 910 × 56. Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 910 × 56 = 4560. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 15: 4560 = 34 sq m.

items.q: Each thick square is 1 sq ft. Each tile is 16 sq ft. What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: The shaded rectangle is 5 tiles across and 4 tiles down: 5 × 4 = 20 tiles of 16 sq ft, which is 206 sq ft. Check with the side lengths: Change to fractions: 2 12 = 52 (2 × 2 + 1 = 5), 1 13 = 43 (1 × 3 + 1 = 4). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 52 × 43 = 206. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 2: 206 = 103. 10 ÷ 3 = 3 R 1, so 103 = 3 13 sq ft.

items.q: Each thick square is 1 sq m. Each tile is 14 sq m. What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: The shaded rectangle is 3 tiles across and 3 tiles down: 3 × 3 = 9 tiles of 14 sq m, which is 94 sq m. Check with the side lengths: Change to fractions: 1 12 = 32 (1 × 2 + 1 = 3), 1 12 = 32 (1 × 2 + 1 = 3). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 32 × 32 = 94. 9 ÷ 4 = 2 R 1, so 94 = 2 14 sq m.

items.q: Each thick square is 1 sq yd. Each tile is 18 sq yd. What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: The shaded rectangle is 7 tiles across and 3 tiles down: 7 × 3 = 21 tiles of 18 sq yd, which is 218 sq yd. Check with the side lengths: Change to fractions: 1 34 = 74 (1 × 4 + 3 = 7), 1 12 = 32 (1 × 2 + 1 = 3). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 74 × 32 = 218. 21 ÷ 8 = 2 R 5, so 218 = 2 58 sq yd.

items.q: Each thick square is 1 sq ft. Each tile is 16 sq ft. What is the area of the shaded rectangle?
items.e: The shaded rectangle is 7 tiles across and 3 tiles down: 7 × 3 = 21 tiles of 16 sq ft, which is 216 sq ft. Check with the side lengths: Change to fractions: 2 13 = 73 (2 × 3 + 1 = 7), 1 12 = 32 (1 × 2 + 1 = 3). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 73 × 32 = 216. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 3: 216 = 72. 7 ÷ 2 = 3 R 1, so 72 = 3 12 sq ft.

items.q:
3 × 2 14 = ?
Write the answer in simplest form.
items.e: Change to fractions: 2 14 = 94 (2 × 4 + 1 = 9). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 3 × 94 = 274. 27 ÷ 4 = 6 R 3, so 274 = 6 34. (Or: 3 × 2 = 6 and 3 × 14 = 34, so 6 + 34 = 6 34. Multiply both parts.)

items.q:
1 23 × 35 = ?
Write the answer in simplest form.
items.e: Change to fractions: 1 23 = 53 (1 × 3 + 2 = 5). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 53 × 35 = 1515. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 15: 1515 = 1. Do not multiply the whole numbers and the fractions separately.

items.q:
2 14 × 1 13 = ?
Write the answer in simplest form.
items.e: Change to fractions: 2 14 = 94 (2 × 4 + 1 = 9), 1 13 = 43 (1 × 3 + 1 = 4). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 94 × 43 = 3612. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 12: 3612 = 3. Do not multiply the whole numbers and the fractions separately.

items.q:
1 34 × 27 = ?
Write the answer in simplest form.
items.e: Change to fractions: 1 34 = 74 (1 × 4 + 3 = 7). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 74 × 27 = 1428. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 14: 1428 = 12. Do not multiply the whole numbers and the fractions separately.

items.q: A square tile has sides that are 23 yd long. What is the area of the tile?
items.e: Area of a square = side × side = 23 × 23. Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 23 × 23 = 49. The answer is 49 sq yd.

items.q: A square tile has sides that are 1 12 ft long. What is the area of the tile?
items.e: Area of a square = side × side = 1 12 × 1 12. Change to fractions: 1 12 = 32 (1 × 2 + 1 = 3), 1 12 = 32 (1 × 2 + 1 = 3). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 32 × 32 = 94. 9 ÷ 4 = 2 R 1, so 94 = 2 14 sq ft.

items.q: A rectangle is 4 ft long and 2 34 ft wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width = 4 × 2 34. Change to fractions: 2 34 = 114 (2 × 4 + 3 = 11). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 4 × 114 = 444. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 4: 444 = 11 sq ft.

items.q: A rectangle is 3 13 m long and 35 m wide. What is its area?
items.e: Area = length × width = 3 13 × 35. Change to fractions: 3 13 = 103 (3 × 3 + 1 = 10). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 103 × 35 = 3015. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 15: 3015 = 2 sq m.

items.q: A pancake recipe uses 2 23 cups of milk. Zoe makes 34 of the recipe. How much milk does she use?
items.e: 34 of 2 23 cups: 34 × 2 23. Change to fractions: 2 23 = 83 (2 × 3 + 2 = 8). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 34 × 83 = 2412. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 12: 2412 = 2 cups.

items.q: A hiking trail is 2 12 miles long. Lily has hiked 35 of the trail. How far has she hiked?
items.e: 35 of 2 12 miles: 35 × 2 12. Change to fractions: 2 12 = 52 (2 × 2 + 1 = 5). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 35 × 52 = 1510. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 5: 1510 = 32. 3 ÷ 2 = 1 R 1, so 32 = 1 12 miles.

items.q: A can holds 34 gallon of paint. Omar uses 23 of the paint in the can. How much paint does he use?
items.e: 23 of 34 gallon: 23 × 34. Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 23 × 34 = 612. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 6: 612 = 12 gallon.

items.q: A smoothie recipe needs 34 cup of yogurt. Eli makes 2 12 batches. How much yogurt does he need?
items.e: 2 12 batches of 34 cup: 2 12 × 34. Change to fractions: 2 12 = 52 (2 × 2 + 1 = 5). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 52 × 34 = 158. 15 ÷ 8 = 1 R 7, so 158 = 1 78 cups.

items.q: One lap of the school track is 14 mile. Grace runs 6 12 laps. How far does she run?
items.e: 6 12 laps of 14 mile: 6 12 × 14. Change to fractions: 6 12 = 132 (6 × 2 + 1 = 13). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 132 × 14 = 138. 13 ÷ 8 = 1 R 5, so 138 = 1 58 miles.

items.q: A water jug holds 3 13 liters when it is full. Right now it is 34 full. How much water is in the jug?
items.e: 34 of 3 13 liters: 34 × 3 13. Change to fractions: 3 13 = 103 (3 × 3 + 1 = 10). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 34 × 103 = 3012. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 6: 3012 = 52. 5 ÷ 2 = 2 R 1, so 52 = 2 12 liters.

items.q: Mia has 56 yard of ribbon. She uses 35 of it to wrap a gift. How much ribbon does she use?
items.e: 35 of 56 yard: 35 × 56. Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 35 × 56 = 1530. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 15: 1530 = 12 yard.

items.q: A bag holds 4 23 pounds of flour. Ruby uses 37 of the bag to bake bread. How much flour does she use?
items.e: 37 of 4 23 pounds: 37 × 4 23. Change to fractions: 4 23 = 143 (4 × 3 + 2 = 14). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 37 × 143 = 4221. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 21: 4221 = 2 pounds.

items.q: A movie is 1 12 hours long. The class has watched 23 of it. How many hours have they watched?
items.e: 23 of 1 12 hours: 23 × 1 12. Change to fractions: 1 12 = 32 (1 × 2 + 1 = 3). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 23 × 32 = 66. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 6: 66 = 1 hour.

items.q: A rectangular rug is 2 14 ft long and 1 23 ft wide. What is the area of the rug?
items.e: Area = length × width: 2 14 × 1 23. Change to fractions: 2 14 = 94 (2 × 4 + 1 = 9), 1 23 = 53 (1 × 3 + 2 = 5). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 94 × 53 = 4512. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 3: 4512 = 154. 15 ÷ 4 = 3 R 3, so 154 = 3 34 sq ft.

items.q: Ava prints a photo that is 4 12 in long and 3 13 in wide. What is the area of the photo?
items.e: Area = length × width: 4 12 × 3 13. Change to fractions: 4 12 = 92 (4 × 2 + 1 = 9), 3 13 = 103 (3 × 3 + 1 = 10). Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 92 × 103 = 906. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 6: 906 = 15 sq in.

items.q: In a class, 23 of the students walk to school. 34 of the walkers walk with a brother or sister. What fraction of the class walks with a brother or sister?
items.e: Find 34 of 23. Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 34 × 23 = 612. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 6: 612 = 12.

items.q: 12 of a pizza was left after dinner. Sofia ate 13 of what was left. What fraction of the whole pizza did she eat?
items.e: Find 13 of 12. Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 13 × 12 = 16. The answer is 16.

items.q: 58 of a park is a field. 25 of the field is a soccer field. What fraction of the park is the soccer field?
items.e: Find 25 of 58. Multiply the tops and the bottoms: 25 × 58 = 1040. Simplify: divide the top and bottom by 10: 1040 = 14.

items.q: There are 24 students in a class. 23 of them play an instrument. 38 of those players play the piano. How many students play the piano?
items.e: 23 of 24: 24 ÷ 3 = 8, 2 × 8 = 16 students play an instrument. 38 of 16: 16 ÷ 8 = 2, 3 × 2 = 6. (Or: 38 × 23 = 14, and 14 of 24 is 6.)

items.q: A bakery made 48 cookies. 58 of them are chocolate chip. 25 of the chocolate chip cookies have nuts. How many cookies have nuts?
items.e: 58 of 48: 48 ÷ 8 = 6, 5 × 6 = 30 chocolate chip cookies. 25 of 30: 30 ÷ 5 = 6, 2 × 6 = 12.

items.q: A school has 1,500 students. 25 of them ride a bus. How many students ride a bus?
items.e: 25 of 1,500: 1,500 ÷ 5 = 300, and 2 × 300 = 600. (300 is only 15, and 900 is the students who do not ride.)

items.q: An orchard has 2,400 trees. 34 of them are apple trees. 23 of the apple trees are red apple trees. How many red apple trees are there?
items.e: 34 of 2,400 is 1,800 apple trees. 23 of 1,800: 1,800 ÷ 3 = 600, 2 × 600 = 1,200. (Or: 23 × 34 = 12, and half of 2,400 is 1,200.)

items.q: Sam practices piano for 34 hour. He spends 23 of that time on scales. How many minutes does he spend on scales?
items.e: 34 hour is 34 of 60 minutes: 60 ÷ 4 = 15, 3 × 15 = 45 minutes. 23 of 45: 45 ÷ 3 = 15, 2 × 15 = 30 minutes.

items.q: Leo's book has 120 pages. He has read 34 of the book. How many pages are left to read?
items.e: 34 of 120: 120 ÷ 4 = 30, 3 × 30 = 90 pages read. Pages left: 120 − 90 = 30. (90 is the pages already read.)
